text:
maya: FYI running into a weird streaming stop/eos issue after HF->Redwood conversion for codegen-1b. Stream sometimes stops mid-character when EOS is a multi-byte sentinel. Repro attached below.

maya: minimal repro snippet (Python):
```
# converted model serving config
model = load_redwood_model('codegen-1b-conv')
resp = model.stream_generate(prompt, stop=["<|eos|>"], max_tokens=128)
for chunk in resp: print(chunk)
# observed: stream breaks and returns incomplete utf-8 char bytes, output truncated early
```

sam: odd — do we know what the tokenizer's eos token is after conversion? HF often maps eos to a multi-char token like "<|endoftext|>" which can be multiple bytes.

sam: can you paste tokenizer.special_tokens_map and tokenizer.encode("<|eos|>") ?

maya: sure. output:
```
special_tokens_map: {"eos_token": "<|eos|>", "bos_token": "<|bos|>"}
# tokenizer.encode('<|eos|>') -> [98812, 2]
# but in the converted tokenizer.json we have "eos_token_id": 98812 and also a sentinel byte sequence present in tokenizer.json.vocab -> split across two token ids
```

jin: my first guess: the streaming stop matcher is doing a byte-sequence substring match on the UTF-8 output buffer, not a token-aware stop detection. If the eos sentinel maps to multiple tokens (like [98812, 2]) and the matcher expects a contiguous byte sequence, it can match only partial bytes and then cut the stream when that partial byte sequence appears in normal output.

jin: two-prong problem: (1) tokenization -> eos is multi-token, (2) stop matcher runs on bytes during streaming. That explains why it sometimes stops mid-utf8 char (because it matched in the middle of a multi-byte encoded token).

maya: that aligns with what I saw. Also noticed the issue spikes when we enable int8 quantization (perf experiments). eval-bot ran a sweep:

eval-bot: quick numbers from the nightly evals (chat stop correctness):
- baseline float16: early-termination rate = 0.9% (N=5k)
- int8 dynamic: early-termination rate = 4.7% (N=5k)
- int8+merge-emb: 3.9%

eval-bot: log samples show truncated UTF-8 at end of chunk and then streaming closes. Looks correlated with batch/buffer alignment after quantized kernel changes.

sam: ugh. Possible fixes:
- make stop-matcher token-aware in streaming path (preferred)
- normalize special tokens at conversion to ensure eos_token is a single token id (merge into one token)
- fall back to post-hoc trimming on the client to only stop at token boundaries

jin: agreed — moving matcher to token-level is safest. Short-term mitigation: when converting HF tokenizer to Redwood format, add a conversion rule to merge multi-token special tokens into a single synthetic token id. CLI flag idea: `--merge-special-tokens`.

maya: wrote a quick patch to conversion that merges contiguous special-token sequences into a single special id. Patch diff (conceptual):
```
# conversion step
if special_tokens sequence maps to multiple token ids:
    create new token "<merged-eos-...>" and set eos_token_id -> new id
    rewrite tokenizer.vocab entries
```
```
# server config patch (hotfix)
streaming:
  stop_matcher: token
  stop_buffer_bytes: 8  # keep small buffer to avoid mid-char cuts
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot noticed new build: redwood/serving@pr-3427 queued for rollout to staging :rocket:

sam: can we add a regression test to catch this? e.g., a streaming-eos test that forces eos -> multi-token and asserts no mid-utf8 truncation.

jin: will add to CI. plan:
- add streaming unit test with a synthetic tokenizer where eos maps to multiple token ids
- feed a prompt that will produce the eos sentinel split across chunks
- assert client-visible output decodes as valid UTF-8 and contains eos sequence exactly once

maya: created PR draft https://git.redwood.internal/pr/3427 (links are internal). Also added a note in model-onboarding checklist: "verify special tokens are single-tokenized or configure streaming to token-mode".

sam: nice. long-term we probably want token-level stop matching + keep conversion opt to merge. Also record quantization regression in release notes.

maya: thanks — workaround in staging looks promising, tests passing locally. I'll follow up after staging rollout. :eyes:

jin: assign me to the CI test and I'll follow up with a benchmark to see if the workaround affects latency.

maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup!
